column2: Revision_Deflation_CJT_and_Kohn-Sham: checks of the dark-matter estimates on the deflating spacetime

column4: the estimates of degeneracy and of condensation in halos contain no coupling: fermions with eight internal states are degenerate in the core of a dwarf galaxy only below 0.276 keV, bound pairs are condensed there only below 262 eV. Computed again; every number agrees with the file of the main project (the masses do not change along the deflation)

self-interaction of bound pairs: with the coupling of today the table of the main project is reproduced (smallest fermion mass 918 MeV for alpha_VS = 0.1). The smallest mass falls as alpha_VS^(-2/3), that is, as exp(-2 tau_d/3) along the deflation. For a given particle the masses m and m_s are constant, hence so is the cross-section 8 pi/m_s^2 of the pairs; the deflation changes whether the pair exists: it is bound only after D_VS = alpha_VS m/m_s has grown to 1.67981

the moment at which the pair becomes bound is a zero-energy resonance of the scattering of two fermions: the scattering length diverges at D_VS = D_c. For a particle with m = 918 MeV and m_s = 54.7 MeV the cross-section per mass at the relative velocities 10, 156 and 1000 km/s rises from 8.4e-1, 8.4e-1, 8.4e-1 cm^2/g one unit of the deflation clock before the binding to the peak values 1.3e7, 5.2e4, 1.3e3 cm^2/g (limit of unitarity at 10 km/s: 1.3e7); it exceeds 100 cm^2/g during an interval of the clock of 0.268, 0.268, 0.258 around the moment of binding. A deflating universe in which the dark matter is made of these fermions passes through an epoch of strong, velocity-dependent self-interaction

growth of structure on the deflating spacetime (A1, A2, A3; data/growth_deflation.csv). The growth depends on the closure of the perturbation equations at the first order in the rate. (i) At a fixed Hubble constant the amplitude of the density contrast today (sigma_8 for a given primordial amplitude) falls with the rate in both closures: d ln sigma_8/d(gsum/H_0) = -0.443 (closure "Momentum") and -0.207 (closure "Pressure"). (ii) The Hubble constant that keeps the angular scale of the sound horizon is lower, the cosmological term takes over later, and matter clusters for longer. With that Hubble constant the net change is d ln sigma_8/d(gsum/H_0) = +0.003 ("Momentum") and +0.239 ("Pressure"): +0.001 and +0.077 per cent at the rate that lunar laser ranging allows, +0.01 and +1.60 per cent at the rate that nucleosynthesis allows. The growth rate f_growth = d ln delta_m/d ln a today rises in both closures, by the factors 1.0021 and 1.0035 (lunar laser ranging), 1.0463 and 1.0773 (nucleosynthesis). Common to both closures is that, at a fixed angle, the amplitude does not fall and the growth rate rises; how large these changes are, and whether the amplitude changes at all, depends on which perturbations the agent carries that holds the extra scale factors, and is not a prediction of the hypotheses. (iii) The four-dimensional equation delta_m'' + 2 H delta_m' = 4 pi G_N(x4) rho_m delta_m, which an earlier version of this command integrated, is neither closure: it gives d ln sigma_8/d(gsum/H_0) = -0.317 at a fixed Hubble constant and +0.128 at a fixed angle

drift of the quantities (table data/dm_drift.csv): the couplings change by 3.1e-3 of themselves over the age of the universe at the rate that lunar laser ranging allows and by 0.06 at the rate that nucleosynthesis allows; quantities near the threshold of binding move much faster (scattering length at D_VS = 1.5: n = 9.1; binding energy at D_VS = 1.8: n = 30.1), and the gap of a weakly paired state moves as 1/lambda (n = 5 for lambda = 0.2). The masses do not move

the quanta that the deflation creates (7+1; modes that depend on a deflating coordinate): at the present rate that lunar laser ranging allows the temperature of the spectrum is 2.9e-33 K; at the largest rate that any of the three bounds of the cosmological part allows (gsum = 0.234 H_0) it is 2.1e-31 K, and hbar gsum is then 3.4e-37 of a mass of 1 keV. The creation of massive particles is suppressed by exp(-2 pi m/rate_t) with an exponent above 1e37 for every mass above 1 keV: no particles are created today. Creation matters only for an epoch in which the rate was comparable with the masses
